$comment: #EXP-1629: THE Avatar fallback rule every Exponential UI renderer replays (React, Solid, Swift, Compose, gpui), the app's own (packages/design-tokens `avatar`, EXP-698 r4) so an eUI avatar and the app's UserAvatar of one person look the same. `palette` = design-tokens `avatar` in ITS order (append-only, never reorder: the index is what the hash lands on). #EXP-1754: the hue KEY is the person's id, else their name, else their email (trimmed; blank counts as absent), so a widget reporter known only by name or email has one colour on every client; nothing at all = the `Avatar/fallback` recipe colours (muted grey). `keys` pins it (eUI's Avatar: `seed` is the id, `name` the name or email). The key picks `palette[fnv1a32(utf8(key)) % 8]` (`hues` pins the hash: the app's 8-id fixture); the fallback fills with that hue at `fillAlpha` and draws the initials in it at full alpha, no stroke. `initials` pins the letters of `name`: an email reduces to its local part, the rest splits on space . _ - +; two or more parts give their first letters, one part its first two characters; uppercased; nothing = `?`. The recipe sizes the letters at half the diameter, regular weight; a picture wears the `Avatar/image` ring (a hairline in `$color.border`), the IDE's gpui-component Avatar.

keys.case: a member: the id wins over name and email
keys.name: Ada Lovelace

keys.case: a widget reporter known by name
keys.name: Jane Reporter

keys.case: a widget reporter known by email only
an empty id falls through to the name
keys.name: Jane Reporter
